RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND

Tyler Hoffman is a twenty-two-year-old from a suburban Ohio neighborhood. He takes his parents' financial support for granted; they pay for his community college tuition, car insurance, and phone plan without complaint, and he does not treat this as a gift requiring gratitude. He has a pattern of starting new projects with enthusiasm and then losing interest and dropping them: he signed up for a CNA class and quit after three weeks, and he dropped out of a computer science program after mentally checking out for months. He is self-aware about this pattern and acknowledges his privilege, but he has not changed his behavior. He admires people who stick with things, such as his father, who has worked the same sales territory for twenty years, and Roy, a disabled veteran he cares for, who still does his daily exercises. Tyler works as an overnight home-care aide for Roy, performing transfers, medication, and repositioning, and he has come to appreciate the quiet rhythm of third shift. He expresses care through punctuality and practical task completion rather than emotional probing. He is also enrolled in a weekend phlebotomy certificate program, which he treats as something "real." He has a habit of making lists of plans and deadlines but leaving them half-used.

His cultural background is Midwestern and practical, emphasizing weather talk, potluck gatherings, and avoiding direct emotional confrontation. In his relationships, his father leaves decisions open-ended, leaving Tyler to carry guilt if he skips events; his mother quietly files away absences and may mention them offhand later; and neighbors John and the Millers have known him since childhood and ask what he's "doing now," which he finds gently uncomfortable. Historically at these watch parties, he arrives near kickoff, never misses one entirely, but drifts to the porch by the second quarter. He has previously texted his family to back out of plans, citing homework or errands, and they accepted it without pushback. His parental support removes financial pressure to follow through on commitments.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION

On a September Saturday, Tyler's father phones to say that the neighbors are gathering at the house to watch the Ohio State game. He mentions that John is bringing chili and the Millers are bringing meatballs, then suggests, "Grab a twelve-pack or a bag of chips if you want." The watch party has unwritten rules: guests should arrive before kickoff, make small talk during commercials, bring a contribution, and not slip out early. Empty-handed guests are noticed in the neighborhood, as is obvious disinterest in the game.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES

Tyler is a few weeks into the phlebotomy certificate program and is unsure whether weekend classes will stick while he works third shift. He is running short on sleep from the week's overnight shifts. He had planned to spend the afternoon reviewing the phlebotomy course schedule online and running errands, which include picking up the course textbook. The invitation immediately brings to mind last year's party, when he arrived with pretzels and his mother handed him the chip bowl so he would look prepared. Also comes to mind his father's rule that no one answers their phone during the first half of the game.
